commit.message:
fix(demo): cleanup-provenance ordering snapshot before teardown (o23) (#118)

* fix(demo): cleanup-provenance ordering snapshot before teardown (o23)

Owned-but-auto-collected containers are accounted instead of failing
preparation=1: capture the Core non-mutating --json inventory once, retry
the native ps inventory with backoff, and record daemon-reported
exited/dead containers as accounted. Add regression test proving the
destroy count is measured pre-teardown. Cites o22-cleanup-prov.md.

* fix(demo): verify pinned Core SHA serveable before checkout (avoid +refs/heads refspec abort)

* fix(demo): commit every qualifying owned container in owned_containers

The o23 restructure of owned_containers() kept only the last matching
row per project, dropping the first of two owned containers in the same
project and raising 'canonical runtime resources lack verified native
ownership' -> exit 1, neither ID unpaused. Now every qualifying row of a
project is committed while preserving the ambiguity guard and the
snapshot-retry/backoff. Adds a two-owned-in-one-project regression case
that fails on the prior head and passes here.

* fix(demo): enforce exact accounting equality in runtime diagnostics (MERGE-118-G)

The accounting guard previously rejected only when accounted_missing was empty,
allowing a pass whenever any single resource was auto-collected even if another
preview resource was a genuine ownership gap, and never detecting an accounted
container that was also natively verified. Replace it with the MERGE-118-G
exact-equality contract: the accounted set and the set of verified-native-owned
containers must cover the preview exactly with no overlap. Each accounted
reason's trailing KEY (PROJECT/NAME or native id) is extracted and compared;
an overlap or any unexplained gap is a hard failure. Add two gating regression
cases.

---------

Co-authored-by: Flash <flash@baseharbor.local>
